title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator.

RESULTS: Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73, p = 0.001; Gray's test p < 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98, p = 0.17; Gray's test p = 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68, p = 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86, p = 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not.

CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01073-w.

Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified.

title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis.
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12-24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers.

RESULTS: Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P_interaction=0.028).

CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease and the heart: how trained immunity shapes cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing intestinal inflammatory disorder. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in patients with IBD, with elevated risks of myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, and venous thromboembolism that are independent of traditional risk factors. Disease activity and histological inflammation independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events, and Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis differ in cardiovascular risk profiles. This residual risk points to immune mechanisms that remain unclear. Trained immunity (TI), an innate immune memory induced by epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, may link chronic intestinal inflammation to cardiovascular injury. This review integrates epidemiological and mechanistic evidence, outlines cardiovascular risk features in IBD, examines the molecular basis of TI and its roles in atherosclerosis, myocardial injury, and heart failure, and evaluates candidate biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. We also discuss current limitations and challenges in clinical translation and propose future research directions, to inform mechanistic studies and clinical interventions for IBD-associated CVD.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty.

METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models.

RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05).

CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort.

title: Early venous filling is associated with unfavorable outcomes in acute basilar artery occlusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between early venous filling (EVF) on digital subtraction angiography and poor outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected. Candidate predictors were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Four variables (fasting blood glucose, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, EVF, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score) were included in Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression models for postprocedural malignant cerebellar edema (MCE) and poor prognosis (90-day modified Rankin Scale score > 2). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with internal validation by bootstrap optimism correction using 1,000 resamples.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 26 (25.7 %) had EVF, 29 (28.7 %) developed MCE, and 56 (55.4 %) had poor prognosis. With four predictors, the events-per-variable values were 7.25 for MCE and 11.25 for poor prognosis, using the smaller outcome category. EVF was associated with MCE (OR 34.650, 95 % CI 9.024-184.087; P < 0.001) and poor prognosis (OR 10.239, 95 % CI 2.889-54.718; P < 0.001) in the Firth models. For MCE, the apparent AUCs of the clinical model and the clinical model plus EVF were 0.804 and 0.944, respectively; the corresponding optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 and 0.926. For poor prognosis, the apparent AUCs were 0.762 and 0.836, and the optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.742 and 0.818. The optimism-corrected AUC increments with EVF were 0.138 for MCE and 0.076 for poor prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: EVF was independently associated with MCE and poor prognosis after MT in patients with ABAO.

title: Clinical significance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index in glycemic control and ischemic limb damage in type 2 diabetes with chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical relevance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) complicated by chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) .

METHODS: A total of 520 patients with CLTI were collected and divided into two groups based on the history of T2DM: the combined T2DM group and the non-T2DM group. The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed.

RESULTS: The CTI in the combined T2DM group was significantly greater than that in the non-T2DM group (P < 0.001). The CTI in the poorly controlled blood glucose group was significantly greater than that in the well controlled blood glucose group (P < 0.001). Regardless of whether CLTI patients had T2DM, the CTI in the overweight group was greater than that in the non-overweight group (P < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the CTI discriminating the high wound, ischemia, and foot infection (WIfI) classification was 0.813 (P < 0.001). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses showed that an increased CTI was an independently associated factor for the high WIfI classification in CLTI patients (OR = 6.409, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with CLTI and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

CONCLUSIONS: The CTI was closely related to the presence of T2DM, blood glucose control level, and overweight status in CLTI patients. The CTI has certain clinical value in discriminating the degree of ischemia in CLTI, and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO.

METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.

RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted P<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]).

CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required.

title: Whole-Genome Sequencing and Single-Cell Transcriptomics Identify Human Leukocyte Antigen Loci and a COG5 Variant in Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection (AD) is a lethal cardiovascular emergency with a complex and underexplored genetic basis.

METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci. To pinpoint functional candidates, we integrated epigenomic profiles and single-cell transcriptomes from human aortic tissues.

RESULTS: Whole-genome sequencing analysis identified 21 candidate common loci and 2 low-frequency variants associated with AD in this discovery cohort. Two candidate common variants in the human leukocyte antigen region (rs9260945 near HLA-A and rs9276409 within HLA-DQA2) showed strong associations and colocalized with regulatory elements in aortic and immune cells, indicating immune-mediated vascular pathology. A low-frequency missense variant in the COG5 gene (rs1203229795, effect allele frequency=0.019) emerged as an independent AD risk factor, likely affecting extracellular matrix glycosylation. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of AD-associated variants in human aortic tissues demonstrated enhanced interactions among fibroblasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and macrophages, supporting their roles in AD pathogenesis. Integrated gene-based and expression analyses further highlighted TPM4, a marker of vascular smooth muscle cell dedifferentiation, as a putative susceptibility gene in AD.

CONCLUSIONS: This multiomics investigation expands the genetic landscape of sporadic AD in Chinese individuals, revealing immune-related human leukocyte antigen loci and a functionally supported candidate COG5 variant. Our findings offer new insights into AD pathogenesis and identify candidate targets for future diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: We performed whole-genome sequencing on 151 patients with sporadic Stanford type B AD and 965 healthy controls in a Chinese population as a discovery phase analysis to assess both common and rare variants. Cross-ancestry meta-analyses incorporating 4 external genome-wide association data sets were used to identify population-specific risk loci.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited.

METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12.

DISCUSSION: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.Clinical Trial Registration: http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population.

title: Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction Models for Peripheral Artery Disease: A Nationally Representative Analysis of NHANES 1999-2004.
abstract: BackgroundWe evaluated the association between small dense low-density lipoprotein (sdLDL) and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and developed prediction models using NHANES 1999-2004.MethodsThis weighted cross-sectional study included 3,415 participants (3,227 without PAD and 188 with PAD). PAD was defined by ankle-brachial index (ABI) <0.90; participants with ABI ≥1.40 or missing ABI were excluded. Survey-weighted logistic regression assessed the association between sdLDL and PAD. For machine learning, complete-case data (n=2,828) were split into training (70%) and test (30%) sets before feature selection and preprocessing. Correlation screening, LASSO, encoding, standardization, and SMOTE were restricted to the training set. Nine algorithms were evaluated using discrimination and calibration metrics.ResultssdLDL was not independently associated with PAD in the fully adjusted model (OR=1.01, 95% CI 0.94-1.10, P=0.69). LASSO retained eight predictor domains: age, body mass index, C-reactive protein, education, estimated glomerular filtration rate, hypertension, poverty-income ratio, and smoking. In the test set, gradient boosting machine achieved the highest AUC (0.833, 95% CI 0.777-0.889), followed by logistic regression (0.819) and XGBoost (0.811). SHAP analysis highlighted age, eGFR, and smoking-related variables as important contributors.Conclusions: sdLDL was not independently associated with PAD. Several models showed acceptable discrimination, with GBM performing numerically best and logistic regression remaining competitive. External validation in contemporary cohorts is required.

title: Risk-benefit profile of upper versus lower extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal insertion site for peripherally inserted central catheters in neonates remains uncertain. International guidelines differ in their recommendations regarding upper- versus lower-extremity placement, and existing systematic reviews are limited by small samples, narrow outcome coverage, or outdated evidence.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the potential risk-benefit profile of upper- versus lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 6, 2026, for studies comparing upper- versus lower-extremity placement in neonates. Primary outcomes were venous thromboembolism, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter tip malposition; secondary outcomes included phlebitis, catheter migration, catheter leakage, catheter occlusion, catheter breakage, total complications, dwell time, unplanned removal, pericardial or pleural effusion, sepsis, and all-cause mortality. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Crude estimates were pooled, sparse and heterogeneous adjusted estimates were summarised narratively, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.

RESULTS: Twenty-one observational studies from 10 countries, involving 15,289 catheters, were included. For primary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism (RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; P = 0.017; low certainty) but higher risks of central line-associated bloodstream infection (RR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.95; P = 0.018; very low certainty) and catheter tip malposition (RR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.61-4.30; P < 0.001; very low certainty). For secondary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with lower phlebitis risk (RR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.94; P = 0.022; low certainty) but higher risks of catheter migration (RR = 1.74, 95% CI 1.27-2.38; P < 0.001; low certainty), catheter leakage (RR = 2.24, 95% CI 1.35-3.73; P = 0.002; moderate certainty), and a marginally higher risk of unplanned removal (RR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.00-1.51; P = 0.048; very low certainty). A post hoc exploratory analysis suggested a possible higher risk of pericardial or pleural effusion (RR = 3.79, 95% CI 1.20-12.02; P = 0.024; very low certainty). No statistically significant between-site differences were observed for other secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Crude observational evidence suggested a potential bidirectional risk-benefit profile across catheter-related outcomes. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because non-randomised designs remain susceptible to residual confounding. The observed associations may inform risk-informed, individualised site selection but do not establish a universally preferred site. Prospective studies with standardised outcomes and adjusted analyses are needed.

title: [Predictive value and threshold effect analysis of the novel systemic immune-inflammatory complex index for functional outcomes at 90 days after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore the correlation between the baseline systemic immune-inflammatory complex index (SIICI) and the 90-day functional prognosis of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) undergoing reperfusion therapy, as well as the threshold effect.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled. Patients were divided into good prognosis group [modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score was 0-2] and a poor prognosis group (mRS score was 3-6) according to the 90-day score after onset. The clinical data and blood routine indicators within 24 hours after onset were collected, and SIICI and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) were calculated. Univariate Logistic regression analysis was performed to screen 90-day functional prognosis-related influencing factors in patients with AIS after reperfusion therapy. Multivariate Logistic regression with multi-gradient adjustment was used to determine whether SIICI was an independent risk factor for poor functional prognosis or not. The restricted cubic spline (RCS) model was applied to analyze the dose-response relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor functional prognosis, and piecewise linear regression model was used for threshold effect analysis. Subjects were randomly divided into a training set and a validation set at a ratio of 7 : 3 for constructing a prognostic prediction model based on SIICI and internal validation. The receiver operator characteristic curve (ROC curve), calibration curve and decision curve analysis (DCA) were plotted to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical net benefit of the model.

RESULTS: All 1 919 AIS patients were enrolled in the final analysis, including 1 176 cases (61.28%) in the good prognosis group and 743 cases (38.72%) in the poor prognosis group. Univariate Logistic regression analysis showed that advanced age, history of atrial fibrillation, bridging therapy, endovascular thrombectomy, elevated baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score, prolonged total length of hospital stay, increased white blood cell count, elevated neutrophil count, elevated monocyte count, increased SII and elevated SIICI were risk factors for poor 90-day functional prognosis of AIS patients, and the history of hyperlipidemia and elevated lymphocyte count were protective factors (all P<0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression analysis demonstrated that after adjusting for gender, age, past medical history, Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification and baseline NIHSS score, SIICI remained an independent risk factor for poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients [odds ratio (OR)=1.008, 95% confidence interval (95%CI) was 1.001-1.014, P=0.022], whereas SII showed no statistical significance after adjustment (OR=1.010, 95%CI was 0.999-1.020, P=0.067), suggesting that SIICI possessed better stability of independent association than the traditional inflammatory index SII. The RCS model verified a significant non-linear relationship between SIICI and the risk of poor 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients (P<0.001). The optimal inflection point value of SIICI determined by piecewise linear regression was 15.03. When SIICI<15.03, each one-unit increase in SIICI was associated with an 11% increased risk of poor functional prognosis (OR=1.112, 95%CI was 1.078-1.147, P<0.001). When SIICI≥15.03, no statistically significant correlation was observed between SIICI and poor functional prognosis (OR=1.005, 95%CI was 0.998-1.012, P=0.136). For the SIICI-based prognosis prediction model, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) was 0.656 (95%CI was 0.626-0.686) in the training set and 0.639 (95%CI was 0.593-0.686) in the validation set, indicating favorable prognostic discrimination ability. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test yielded P=0.064, suggesting good model calibration. DCA revealed that the model obtained significant clinical net benefit within the high-risk threshold range of 0-0.8.

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline SIICI is independently correlated with the 90-day functional prognosis in AIS patients after reperfusion therapy and shows a significant threshold effect. It exhibits superior predictive performance compared with the traditional inflammatory index SII. The prognostic prediction model constructed based on SIICI can assist clinicians in stratifying the risk of early functional prognosis in patients with AIS undergoing reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 1 919 AIS patients who received reperfusion therapy and were admitted to The First Affiliated Hospital of University of Science and Technology of China from January 1, 2022 to December 31, 2025 were enrolled.

title: Longitudinal monitoring of adalimumab levels and anti-adalimumab antibodies in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the association between longitudinal adalimumab concentrations, anti-adalimumab antibodies (AAA) levels, and clinical response in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS).

METHODS: A prospective multi-center, observational cohort study of AS patients receiving adalimumab therapy was conducted. Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization. Adalimumab concentrations were measured using a validated sandwich immunoassay. Measurement of AAA levels was performed with a laboratory-developed immunoassay system integrating electrochemiluminescence technology with specific immunomagnetic separation, with result reported as signal-to-noise ratio (S/N).

RESULTS: A total of 140 patients receiving adalimumab monotherapy were included. The median follow-up period was 169 days, and 711 plasma samples were available for adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels measurements. Seven patients had pre-existing AAA, and 120 (90.2%) of the remaining 133 patients tested positive for AAA during follow-up. A total of 48 patients were excluded from the exposure-response relationship dataset owing to pre-existing AAA (n=7), lack of active disease (n=26), incomplete follow-up (n=8), and prolonged dosing intervals (n=7). Among the remaining 92 patients, a total of 58 (63%) achieved clinical response. Adalimumab concentrations were higher, and AAA levels were significantly lower, in responders compared with non-responders at multiple time points. Exposure-response relationship models also revealed a steady-state adalimumab concentration target of 5.1 μg/mL and a week-4 concentration target of 3.3 μg/mL, corresponding to an 80% probability of clinical response. Thirty-six of 92 patients (39.1%) exhibited AAA-S/N values exceeding the putative clinically meaningful threshold (AAA-S/N=10). Patients in the high-AAA group (AAA-S/N≥10) had lower drug levels (median: 1.5 μg/mL vs. 6.9 μg/mL, P<0.0001) and poorer response rates (38.8% vs. 78.6%, P = 0.0002), relative to those in the low-AAA group (AAA-S/N<10). Furthermore, patients who were week-4 AAA-positive exhibited a 1.8-fold increased risk of non-response (relative risk, 95% confidence interval, 1.1-2.8).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that longitudinal profiles of adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels show a strong association with clinical responses in this Chinese AS cohort, which may inform therapeutic drug monitoring-guided adalimumab treatment strategies that remain to be further validated.

Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization.

title: Dichloroacetate mitigates experimental abdominal aortic aneurysm via suppression of CXCL5-mediated neutrophil chemotaxis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease with high rupture-associated mortality. Current management relies on surgical or endovascular repair, with no effective pharmacological therapy. Inflammation and immune cell infiltration are central to AAA pathogenesis, but the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined.

METHODS: Human AAA tissues and murine AAA models (CaCl2 and porcine pancreatic elastase) were analyzed for chemokine expression and immune cell infiltration. The role of CXCL5 was investigated using immunohistochemistry, RNA-seq, and flow cytometry. The pharmacological effects of dichloroacetate (DCA), a pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase inhibitor, were assessed in vitro in smooth muscle cells and in vivo in AAA models.

RESULTS: CXCL5 was markedly enriched in human AAA lesions and associated with neutrophil infiltration. In murine AAA, neutrophil accumulation was evident and correlated with CXCL5 expression. DCA treatment suppressed ROS generation and NF-κB activation in smooth muscle cells, thereby reducing CXCL5 expression. Functionally, DCA significantly attenuated AAA formation in both CaCl2- and elastase-induced models. Mechanistically, DCA mitigated AAA progression by inhibiting CXCL5-mediated neutrophil chemotaxis.

CONCLUSION: CXCL5-driven neutrophil recruitment is a key mechanism in AAA pathogenesis. DCA suppresses CXCL5 expression through inhibition of oxidative stress and NF-κB signaling, conferring protection against experimental AAA. These findings highlight CXCL5 as a potential therapeutic target and establish DCA as a promising candidate drug for AAA treatment.

Current management relies on surgical or endovascular repair, with no effective pharmacological therapy. Inflammation and immune cell infiltration are central to AAA pathogenesis, but the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined.

title: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty for occlusive lesions of pulmonary artery in Takayasu arteritis: A cohort study.
abstract: BackgroundOcclusive pulmonary arterial lesions represent a major technical challenge for balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) in patients with Takayasu arteritis-associated pulmonary artery involvement. However, evidence and procedural guidance regarding BPA for occlusive lesions in this population remain limited.ObjectivesThis study aimed to summarize our center experience with BPA for occlusive pulmonary arterial lesions in patients with Takayasu arteritis and to identify potential risk factors associated with restenosis after BPA.DesignRetrospective cohort.MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled patients with Takayasu arteritis who had occlusive pulmonary arterial lesions. Lesions were morphologically categorized as subtotal or total occlusions. Total occlusions were further subclassified as cone-shaped, pouch-like, or ostial occlusions.ResultsWe included 66 patients with Takayasu arteritis, in whom 182 occlusive lesions were identified. In terms of locations, most ostial occlusions (56.52%) located lobar, while other kinds of lesions more common located segmentally. Total occlusions more frequently required guide-extension catheter support than subtotal occlusions (70.21% vs. 40.63%, P<0.001). Hard-tip guidewires were required for revascularization in 53.85% of ostial occlusions, compared with only 3.13% of subtotal occlusions. Lesion-level technical success rates among attempted lesions decreased with increasing lesion complexity: 100% for subtotal occlusions, 96.0% for cone-shaped occlusions, 68.4% for pouch-like occlusions, and 43.8% for ostial occlusions. The corresponding recanalization rates among all identified lesions were 78.69%, 88.9%, 52.04%, and 10.14%, respectively. In exploratory univariable Firth penalized logistic regression, irregular anticoagulation was associated with a higher likelihood of restenosis (OR 8.51, 95% CI 1.39-60.91; P=0.021), whereas baseline hemodynamics were not associated with restenosis.ConclusionThe techniques and devices illustrated in this study might guide the BPA performance in addressing occlusive lesions.

title: Prognostic Value of the Pan-Immune Inflammatory Value and Fibrinogen-To-Albumin Ratio for Amputation in Patients With Lower Extremity Arterial Disease.
abstract: BackgroundLower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) remains a major cause of amputation, even after successful endovascular revascularization therapy (EVT). The prognostic associations of the pan-immune inflammatory value (PIV) and fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) in LEAD remain unclear. This study investigated the associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk and evaluated their incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical variables.MethodsIn this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 1,082 patients with LEAD who underwent EVT at four tertiary hospitals in Southwest China between January 2018 and July 2023 were analyzed. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses and Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate the associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk. Exploratory cut-off values were derived using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The incremental prognostic value of adding PIV and FAR to clinical variables was assessed using time-dependent ROC analysis.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 31 months, 198 (18.3%) patients experienced amputation. RCS revealed significant nonlinear associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk (p for nonlinearity < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, higher levels of both biomarkers remained independently associated with increased amputation risk (Z-PIV: HR = 1.379; Z-FAR: HR = 1.176; both p < 0.001). The addition of PIV and FAR to the clinical model enhanced time-dependent discrimination; the AUC(t) increased from 0.771 to 0.819 at 1 year, 0.766 to 0.806 at 2 years, and 0.762 to 0.807 at 3 years (all adjusted p < 0.001). Fine-Gray competing-risk analyses yielded consistent results after accounting for death as a competing event.ConclusionPIV and FAR were independently associated with amputation risk in patients with LEAD who underwent EVT. The addition of these biomarkers to established clinical variables provided incremental prognostic value and may offer additional prognostic information for risk stratification.

title: Uterine Artery Embolization Combined with Hysteroscopic Surgery for the Treatment of Complex Submucosal Leiomyomas with Refractory Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Submucosal uterine fibroids are a common structural cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in women of reproductive age. Transcervical resection of myoma (TCRM), as the standard procedure, still faces many challenges in the management of cases with rich blood supply or rapid growth.

CASE DATA: We report a case of a young nulliparous patient who developed recurrent acute massive haemorrhage one month after the initial TCRM due to complex submucosal fibroids, which failed to respond to medication. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated that branches of the left uterine artery directly supplied the lesion. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) was then performed, and a second TCRM was performed after embolization to achieve complete resection of the lesion. Review of the initial postoperative pathology revealed increased tumor cellularity with focal proliferative activity. The Ki-67 index in hot-spot areas was about 10%, indicating active cell proliferation. The final diagnosis was cellular leiomyoma. After nearly 6 months of follow-up, the patient's menstruation returned to normal, but long-term outcomes such as reproductive function still require longer-term follow-up.

CONCLUSION: This case indicates that the combination of UAE and TCRM achieves a favorable short‑term outcome in the treatment of hypervascular submucosal fibroids complicated with intractable acute hemorrhage. Given the limitations of the single‑case study and the relatively short follow‑up duration, the long‑term efficacy and fertility preservation outcomes remain to be further verified. Individualized clinical decision‑making and prolonged follow‑up are therefore recommended.

Transcervical resection of myoma (TCRM), as the standard procedure, still faces many challenges in the management of cases with rich blood supply or rapid growth. CASE DATA: We report a case of a young nulliparous patient who developed recurrent acute massive haemorrhage one month after the initial TCRM due to complex submucosal fibroids, which failed to respond to medication.

title: Age-dependent associations of peripheral immune-inflammatory indices with cerebrovascular remodeling after revascularization in ischemic moyamoya disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Peripheral immune-inflammatory activity may influence postoperative vascular remodeling in Moyamoya disease (MMD), but the relevant pathways may differ by developmental stage. We investigated age-dependent associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory indices with two complementary imaging outcomes: collateralization angiogenesis ratio (CAR) and arterial residual volume (ARV).

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 108 patients with ischemic MMD who underwent revascularization (76 adults and 32 pediatric patients). Associations of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR), and platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR) with CAR and ARV were screened using Spearman correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Standardized multivariable linear models used HC3 robust standard errors and adjusted for age, sex, Suzuki stage, and follow-up. Effect modification was evaluated using cohort-by-marker and continuous age-by-marker interactions.

RESULTS: CAR and ARV did not differ between adults and pediatric patients (P = 0.583 and P = 0.853, respectively) and were uncorrelated within either cohort, supporting their interpretation as distinct remodeling dimensions. In unadjusted analyses, pediatric NPR correlated inversely with CAR (ρ=-0.431, P = 0.014), whereas adult PLR correlated inversely with ARV (ρ=-0.242, P = 0.035); neither association survived false-discovery-rate correction. After adjustment, pediatric NPR remained inversely associated with CAR (standardized β=-0.380, 95% CI -0.652 to -0.108; P = 0.006). The adult PLR-ARV association was borderline (β=-0.255, 95% CI -0.512 to 0.002; P = 0.052). PLR showed significant age-dependent effect modification: the PLR pediatric-cohort interaction was positive (β=0.547, 95% CI 0.112 to 0.981; P = 0.014), and the PLR continuous-age interaction was negative (β=-0.264, 95% CI -0.485 to -0.043; P = 0.019), indicating that the PLR-ARV relationship became more negative with increasing age.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, peripheral inflammatory indices were associated with different postoperative remodeling pathways according to developmental stage. The age-dependent PLR-ARV relationship was the most consistent interaction signal, whereas the adjusted pediatric NPR-CAR association suggests a potentially localized collateralization mechanism. However, these exploratory findings require validation in larger, prospectively characterized cohorts.

We investigated age-dependent associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory indices with two complementary imaging outcomes: collateralization angiogenesis ratio (CAR) and arterial residual volume (ARV). METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 108 patients with ischemic MMD who underwent revascularization (76 adults and 32 pediatric patients).

title: Pulmonary embolism as the initial manifestation of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in an adolescent: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is uncommon in adolescents and often presents with non-specific symptoms, which may delay diagnosis. Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a recognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism; however, thromboembolic events may occasionally precede overt renal manifestations, creating additional diagnostic challenges.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 17-year-old male adolescent with steroid-responsive NS initially presenting with PE. The patient initially developed fever, cough, and abdominal pain, leading to a preliminary diagnosis of pneumonia and cholecystitis before PE was identified. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography revealed bilateral multiple pulmonary emboli. Laboratory evaluation showed hypoalbuminemia, but initial repeated urinalyses were negative for proteinuria and renal function was preserved. During hospitalization, the patient developed edema, acute kidney injury, and nephrotic-range proteinuria. No definite evidence of secondary NS was identified. Renal biopsy was not performed due to concurrent anticoagulation therapy and refusal from the patient's family. His symptoms improved after anticoagulation and glucocorticoid therapy, and there was no recurrence during a two-year follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights two important diagnostic challenges: PE should be considered even in adolescents with non-specific symptoms, and NS may remain clinically silent when thromboembolic events occur, particularly in patients with unexplained PE accompanied by hypoalbuminemia.

Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a recognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism; however, thromboembolic events may occasionally precede overt renal manifestations, creating additional diagnostic challenges. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 17-year-old male adolescent with steroid-responsive NS initially presenting with PE.

title: [Imaging-Guided Percutaneous Superior Vena Cava Catheterization for Hemodialysis Access in Patients With Thoracic Central Vein Obstruction].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety and feasibility of percutaneous superior vena cava (SVC) catheterization in patients with thoracic central vein obstruction (TCVO) and to assess the accuracy of preprocedural multi-detector computed tomography venography (MDCTV) in predicting SVC puncture angles.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 106 patients who underwent percutaneous SVC catheterization for TCVO between January 2020 and December 2023. Patient baseline characteristics, surgical data, and follow-up information were collected. Preprocedural MDCTV images were analyzed using OsiriX, a medical imaging interpretation and processing software, to determine predicted puncture angles. A paired-sample t-test was used to examine the agreement between MDCTV-predicted puncture angle and the actual puncture angle measured by intraoperative digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Technical success rates and perioperative complication rates were recorded, and catheter patency rates were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

RESULTS: Among the 106 patients, 78.3% (83/106) had type 2B TCVO and 19.8% (21/106) had type 3 TCVO. The technical success rate of the procedure was 100% (106/106), and the incidence of severe complications was 1.9% (2/106). There were no statistically significant differences between the preprocedural MDCTV-predicted and intraoperative DSA-measured puncture angles in the coronal plane (11.46° vs 11.37°, P = 0.977) or the sagittal plane (18.62° vs 17.12°, P = 0.848). Catheter patency rates were 98.1% at 14 days and 80% at 24 months.

CONCLUSION: Percutaneous SVC catheterization is a safe and effective vascular access salvage option for patients with TCVO when conventional vascular access options have been exhausted. Preprocedural MDCTV can effectively predict SVC puncture angles, providing an objective basis for preprocedural route planning, thereby reducing operative risks and improving technical success rates.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 106 patients who underwent percutaneous SVC catheterization for TCVO between January 2020 and December 2023. Patient baseline characteristics, surgical data, and follow-up information were collected.

title: Prior-driven multimodal contrastive learning with Fourier cross-attention to detect aortic dissection in 3D non-contrast CT.
abstract: Accurate identification of aortic dissection (AD) in emergencies is clinically critical. Non-contrast CT (NC-CT), the standard emergency imaging for chest pain, has limited AD diagnostic sensitivity. We developed an anatomy prior-driven multimodal contrastive learning framework, extracting discriminative features from contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) and radiological reports to enhance NC-CT-based AD detection. Aortic segmentation and straightening focus analysis on relevant anatomy, while our tri-encoder architecture leverages Fourier cross-attention (core innovation) to co-extract spatial and frequency-domain features with hybrid contrastive-focal frequency loss. After pre-training, only NC-CT is needed for inference. Evaluated on 134 subjects (70 AD, 64 non-AD), our method achieved 0.955 accuracy and 0.983 AUC, outperforming 9 SOTA models. External validation showed 0.933 accuracy, with lumen segmentation reaching an average Dice score of 0.773. These results demonstrate that our method can advance AD detection and enable accurate true/false lumen localization using NC-CT alone.

title: Covered stent placement in the management of superior vena cava lesions in hemodialysis patients: A retrospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior vena cava lesions represent a challenging complication of central venous catheter use in maintenance hemodialysis patients. While endovascular intervention is the first-line treatment, restenosis rates remain high with plain balloon angioplasty and bare-metal stents. Covered stents have emerged as a potential alternative, yet data on their long-term efficacy in this specific population are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To analyze the clinical characteristics of hemodialysis patients with SVC lesions and evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of covered stent placement in treating these lesions.

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: The chi-squared or Fisher's exact test was used for categorical variables. For continuous variables, normality was assessed by the Shapiro-Wilk test; normally distributed data were compared using Welch's t-test with Hedges' g and 95% CI, and non-normally distributed data using the Mann-Whitney U test with r values and 95% CI.

RESULTS: A total of 24 patients were included. The main clinical symptoms were facial edema, limb edema, catheter dysfunction, and AVF dysfunction. The lesions were characterized as stenosis in 16 patients (67%) and occlusion in eight patients (33%). Subgroup analysis revealed no significant difference in the number of catheterizations or in total catheter indwelling time between the stenosis and occlusion groups (P > 0.05). However, the occlusion group required more balloons during the intervention (P = 0.016). Complications included intraoperative vascular rupture and arrhythmia. The median follow-up time was 27 months (21, 41), an the primary patency rate of the target lesions was 100%.

CONCLUSION: The use of Viabahn covered stents for treating SVC lesions in hemodialysis patients significantly improved the primary patency rate of target lesions, enhances clinical outcomes, and prolonged patency duration.

While endovascular intervention is the first-line treatment, restenosis rates remain high with plain balloon angioplasty and bare-metal stents. Covered stents have emerged as a potential alternative, yet data on their long-term efficacy in this specific population are limited.

title: Engineering Human Blood Vessel Organoids for Failed Ischemic Repair in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) remains a major cause of nonhealing wounds, tissue loss, amputation, and death despite advances in revascularization. This Review reframes CLTI as failed ischemic vascularized-tissue repair and evaluates how human vascular models can reproduce disease-specific repair failure and test regenerative interventions.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from human CLTI with experimental studies of human blood vessel organoids (BVOs), engineered perfusable microvessels, vascular-on-chip systems, and vascularized tissue models. Direct CLTI observations are distinguished from mechanisms inferred from related ischemic, metabolic, and inflammatory systems. Model requirements and readouts are organized around disease-specific pathological benchmarks.

RESULTS: The synthesis indicates that restoration of macroscopic blood flow may be insufficient when microvascular maturation, tissue perfusion, and reparative remodeling remain defective. CLTI-oriented platforms should therefore reproduce sustained hypoperfusion, heterogeneous hypoxia, metabolic dysfunction, persistent inflammation, diabetes-associated microvascular injury, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and failed vascular maturation. BVOs are best positioned as the vascular core of modular ischemic-limb systems integrated, when required, with skeletal-muscle, wound, stromal, immune, matrix, and neural compartments. The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-lactate-lactylation relationship is presented as a proposed, testable framework connecting oxygen sensing, glycolytic remodeling, lactate accumulation, endothelial and immune plasticity, and unstable vascular repair. A platform-specific roadmap combines patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells, microfluidic perfusion, multicellular coculture, multi-omic profiling, and structural, maturation, functional, durability, and tissue-repair endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: BVO-based and perfusion-enabled vascular platforms can support mechanistic validation, therapeutic and toxicity screening, patient-specific modeling, and vascularized construct design, provided that structural angiogenesis is distinguished from functional and durable tissue rescue.

title: Hemodialysis professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward venous thrombosis prevention: a multicenter survey.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a serious complication in patients undergoing hemodialysis. This cross-sectional study investigated the self-perceived knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) regarding VTE prevention among hemodialysis professionals and explored the factors influencing their preventive practices. Hemodialysis professionals were recruited using convenience sampling, and data were collected via the Wenjuanxing platform using a general information questionnaire and a self-developed KAP questionnaire on VTE prevention. A total of 515 questionnaires were distributed, and 474 valid questionnaires were returned, yielding a valid response rate of 92.03%. The mean total KAP score for VTE prevention was 164.12 ± 27.74, with a standardized score of 71.36 ± 12.06, indicating a moderately high overall level. Self-perceived knowledge, attitude, and practice were correlated with each other (r = 0.389-0.424, p < 0.001). Multivariate stepwise linear regression analysis showed that age, hospital type, hospital level, number of daily dialysis shifts, implementation of VTE risk assessment, awareness of VTE-related guidelines, and training frequency were significant associated factors of the total KAP score, among which the implementation of VTE risk assessment was the most important factor (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that targeted training programs, strengthened clinical management mechanisms, and improved awareness and application of VTE risk assessment are needed to further enhance the standardization and effectiveness of VTE prevention in hemodialysis patients.

title: Cytoreductive Nephrectomy and Thrombectomy for Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma with Venous Tumor Thrombus: Experience from a High-Volume Center.
abstract:
PURPOSE: For metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) with venous tumor thrombus (TT), the role of cytoreductive nephrectomy (CN) remains controversial, particularly in the targeted-immunotherapy era, and East-Asian data are limited.

METHODS: This study retrospectively included 160 East-Asian patients with mRCC with TT who underwent CN and thrombectomy from January 2014 to January 2025. Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses identified prognostic factors. Variables with a p‑value < 0.1 in the univariate analysis were entered into the multivariate analysis. A two‑sided p‑value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Median follow-up was 35 months; median OS was 41 months. Multivariate analysis identified four independent risk factors for poor OS: sarcomatoid differentiation (p < 0.001), serious postoperative complications (p < 0.001), rhabdoid differentiation (p = 0.004), and pathologic lymph node metastasis (p = 0.005). Mayo level was not significantly associated with OS. Robotic surgery demonstrated superior perioperative outcomes to open surgery, although baseline characteristics between the two groups were not comparable.

CONCLUSIONS: Acceptable long-term oncologic outcomes are achievable when CN and thrombectomy are performed in carefully selected surgical patients with mRCC and venous TT. Sarcomatoid differentiation, rhabdoid differentiation, pathologic lymph node metastasis, and postoperative serious complications are independent predictors of poor prognosis. To obtain more reliable perioperative outcome data, robotic surgery should be compared with open surgery in larger patient populations. Multidisciplinary evaluation and centralization of care at high‑volume centers are strongly encouraged.

METHODS: This study retrospectively included 160 East-Asian patients with mRCC with TT who underwent CN and thrombectomy from January 2014 to January 2025. Overall survival (OS) was the primary endpoint.

title: Stent retrievers for acute ischemic stroke: technological advances, clinical applications, and future perspectives.
abstract: Acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusion remains a leading cause of death and disability despite established reperfusion therapies. Although stent retriever-based thrombectomy has become the standard of care, outcomes are still constrained in complex occlusions and anatomically challenging cases. This review summarizes and critically appraises recent advances in stent retriever technology, thrombectomy techniques, and evidence expansion in acute ischemic stroke. Device development has progressed from first-generation retrieval systems to self-expanding stent retrievers and recent integrated retrieval-protection platforms, leading to improved clot engagement, higher first-pass reperfusion, and reduced distal embolization. Parallel refinements in procedural strategies including combined aspiration catheters, balloon guide catheters, and dual-stent techniques have enhanced recanalization efficiency and procedural control. Clinical evidence has extended thrombectomy indications beyond conventional time windows to include posterior circulation occlusion, large infarct cores, and selected medium/distal vessel occlusions under imaging-guided selection. Advances in thrombus characterization, biomaterials, surface engineering, and territory-specific devices are further enabling more tailored mechanical approaches. Nevertheless, fibrin-rich resistant thrombi, embolic complications, vascular injury, and limited high-level evidence for emerging devices remain unresolved challenges. Ongoing integration of engineering innovation and clinical data is expected to support more individualized and safer thrombectomy strategies with improved functional outcomes.

title: Intermittent postmenopausal vaginal bleeding as an indicator of vaginal metastasis from occult renal cell carcinoma with rhabdoid differentiation: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The vagina is an exceptionally rare site for metastatic cancer. This case is reported due to its novelty, highlighting how vaginal metastasis can be the initial presentation of an occult renal carcinoma, particularly a highly aggressive variant with rhabdoid differentiation.

CASE INTRODUCTION: A 58-year-old postmenopausal Han Chinese woman from Guangdong Province, China, presented with intermittent vaginal bleeding. Examination revealed a pedunculated vaginal mass. Pathological and immunohistochemical analysis (positive for PAX8, CAIX, CD10; negative for CK7) confirmed metastatic renal cell carcinoma. Subsequent imaging identified a primary left renal mass with venous tumor thrombi. The patient underwent cytoreductive radical nephrectomy and thrombectomy. Final pathology confirmed clear cell renal cell carcinoma, WHO/ISUP grade 4, with rhabdoid differentiation.

CONCLUSION: This case underscores that a solitary vaginal mass may be a metastasis from an occult malignancy. It highlights the critical importance of considering a metastatic origin in the differential diagnosis, which necessitates a thorough investigation for a primary tumor, as the management and prognosis differ significantly from those of primary gynecological cancer.

This case is reported due to its novelty, highlighting how vaginal metastasis can be the initial presentation of an occult renal carcinoma, particularly a highly aggressive variant with rhabdoid differentiation. title: Iatrogenic axillary arteriovenous fistula complicating permanent pacemaker implantation: successful management with a balloon-expandable covered stent-a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Third-degree atrioventricular block is a class I indication for permanent pacemaker implantation. Iatrogenic axillary arteriovenous fistula is an extremely rare vascular complication of this procedure with limited clinical reports to date.

CASE PRESENTATION: We present the case of a 57-year-old male with third-degree atrioventricular block who developed an axillary arteriovenous fistula during permanent pacemaker implantation via the left axillary vein approach. The complication was promptly diagnosed by emergency axillary arteriography and was successfully occluded with an 8 mm × 37 mm balloon-expandable covered stent. Owing to the ipsilateral vascular injury, the pre‑created left pacemaker pocket was then closed in layers. Permanent pacemaker implantation was subsequently completed uneventfully via the contralateral right axillary vein approach, with a new pacemaker pocket created on the right side. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course and normal pacemaker function at the 1-month follow-up, with no recurrence of symptoms or vascular abnormalities.

CONCLUSIONS: We review the relevant literature, analyze the pathophysiology, diagnosis and interventional management of this rare complication, and propose clinical recommendations for its prevention and acute management, including rational pacemaker pocket management after successful vascular fistula occlusion. This case reinforces the efficacy and safety of balloon-expandable covered stents for iatrogenic axillary arteriovenous fistula and highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration, prompt angiographic diagnosis, and deliberate pocket selection in the management of such acute procedural complications.

title: Direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonists after pulmonary endarterectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension who undergo pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) require lifelong anticoagulation, yet the optimal regimen after surgery remains uncertain. Although vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) are traditionally used, direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have gained attention as potentially safer and more convenient alternatives. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DOACs compared with VKAs in the post-PEA population.

METHODS: We systematically searched three English and four Chinese databases for relevant studies published up to March 2025. Risk of bias was evaluated using RoB 2 for RCTs and ROBINS-I for observational studies. Outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), pulmonary embolism (PE) recurrence, bleeding events, and all-cause mortality. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Five studies (one randomized trial and four observational studies) involving 1986 patients were included. Overall, DOACs did not increase the risk of VTE recurrence compared with VKAs, but were associated with a higher likelihood of PE recurrence (RR = 2.99; 95% CI 1.51-5.93; I2 = 0%). At the same time, patients receiving DOACs experienced fewer major bleeding events (RR = 0.58; 95% CI 0.37-0.91; I2 = 0%) and lower all-cause mortality (RR = 0.51; 95% CI 0.35-0.75; I2 = 0%). Further analyses indicated no significant differences across outcomes in the rivaroxaban-only subgroup, whereas mixed-DOAC regimens were associated with significantly higher risks of both VTE and PE.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients after PEA, DOACs were associated with lower risks of major bleeding and all-cause mortality, but may be less effective than VKAs in preventing PE recurrence. The current evidence-derived largely from observational studies and of low to very low certainty-does not support routine substitution of VKAs with DOACs in this setting. Clinical equipoise therefore remains, and further research is needed to clarify the optimal regimen.

This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of DOACs compared with VKAs in the post-PEA population.
